root_cause.mechanism: LoginAttemptBudget implements Java-faithful FIXED windows ALIGNED to wall-clock epoch minutes: windowStart = floor(now/windowMs)*windowMs (budget.ts:72; windowMs 60_000 hardwired at config.ts:71). The routes test 'successful login clears the account budget (:138)' performs 9 failed logins through REAL bcrypt (~3s wall time, timeout note at routes.test.ts:337) against the REAL systemClock (buildIdentityServices constructs the budget without a clock — config.ts:91-95 — so budget.ts:28 systemClock is used). When the ~3s sequence straddles a wall-minute boundary, recordFailure's insideWindow(existing) check fails for the existing window and a FRESH aligned window opens with count=1 (budget.ts:74-79). currentCount() then reads the NEW window's count (<9) via insideWindow (budget.ts:103-106) and the toBe(9) assertion at routes.test.ts:329 fails. Re-runs that start mid-minute land all 9 failures inside one aligned window and pass — the textbook rare flake (~3-4s exposure per 60s minute ≈ 5-7% per run, matching 2-3 sightings across dozens of suite runs).
root_cause.the_port_is_NOT_the_defect: The window roll is the ported Java law (LoginAttemptBudget.java:61-111 fixed-window semantics; the port doc at budget.ts:15 pins 'window alignment: windowStart = floor(now/window)*window'). The budget clock is injectable BY DESIGN (BudgetClock, budget.ts:24-28 — 'test-visible'). The defect is the test's assumption that wall time cannot cross an aligned boundary mid-test.
root_cause.secondary_exposure: The sibling test 'per-TARGET-account budget: 11 failures → 429 + Retry-After' (routes.test.ts:306) shares the class: its attempts run against the same real systemClock, so a boundary straddle could yield 401 on attempt 11 (fresh window) instead of 429. It passed in run 37294749131 (its 11 unregistered-user attempts take ~309ms — no bcrypt, since budget@example.invalid is never registered — so its exposure is ~0.5%/run) but is fixed by the same clock pin.

fix_design.principle: TEST-ONLY determinism; zero production changes. The port keeps its Java-faithful aligned-window law; the tests stop depending on wall time.
changes: routes.test.ts: add a SteppingClock (BudgetClock impl) seeded at an ALIGNED minute (1_800_000_000_000 % 60_000 === 0) that only advances when advanced.

routes.test.ts: buildTestApp(env, clock?) — when a clock is passed, swap identity.budget for a LoginAttemptBudget constructed WITH that clock BEFORE AuthService construction (AuthService reads identity.budget lazily today — service.ts:154 — but swapping pre-construction is order-safe even against a future eager capture).

routes.test.ts: both budget tests build clock-pinned apps; the 429 test gains an exact deterministic Retry-After pin (value derived from the :110 formula at the pinned instant); the clear test keeps its real-bcrypt cost and 60s timeout (bcrypt parity is worth wall time — the BUDGET clock is what must not be wall-time).

budget.test.ts: one new unit pin — 'a failure in a NEW aligned window starts a fresh count (window roll :66-71)' — enshrines the flake mechanism as Java-faithful law so no future lane 'fixes' the roll and silently breaks parity.
